result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

args.text: When a description says activities happen simultaneously, model them as parallel branches with a parallel gateway. When one activity must follow one branch but is independent of another concurrent activity, keep it on the relevant branch and synchronize the branches before continuing.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already covers the described concurrency and dependency structure.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Only activities, gateways and events are sequence-flow endpoints. Never connect sequence flows to pools, lanes, data objects, groups or annotations.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

result.rule: When the description indicates that an activity recurs at intervals during a longer-running process phase.: Model the recurring activity as work within that phase and connect it to the surrounding process flow.
When the description states that one activity follows another in a specific order.: Model the activities with sequence flows that preserve the stated order.

When the description states that reviews may recur and that feedback from those reviews can lead to changes: Model feedback and change work as explicit activities, and use a decision gateway with a loop to a review when another review may be needed.

When the description states that a recurring process continues until one of multiple distinct outcomes occurs: Model a distinct exit path for each stated outcome and represent each outcome explicitly at termination, rather than collapsing them into an undifferentiated loop exit.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use standard loop or multi-instance characteristics only when repetition is explicit; choose sequential or parallel instances from the description.
Represent loops only when repetition is stated and provide a meaningful exit unless endless behavior is explicit.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
